input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement is Section 3.19, which runs against SFJ (and its Affiliates) during the Exclusive Period (Section 1.1.68) in respect of Competing Products and Brilinta Competing Products. That is exclusivity granted in our favour and is expressly acceptable under the playbook. No provision obliges PB to purchase, source or procure anything exclusively from SFJ or to refrain from using third parties: Section 4.1/4.2 is a funding obligation on SFJ, not a sourcing commitment by PB, and Section 7.5.5 is a consent covenant on out-licensing the Product that expressly carves out Excluded Licensing Transactions, including licences to service providers, CROs and CMOs, so PB remains free to engage alternative suppliers (any restrictive-covenant concern there sits under NONCOMPETE, not this rule). The clause therefore meets the preferred position: PB has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
